title: EBS volumes versus instance store (ephemeral)
hook: Elastic Block Store (EBS) is network-attached durable block storage; instance store is physically local NVMe that disappears when the instance stops or terminates.

blocks.text: Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes attach to EC2 over the network — gp3, io2, st1, sc1 types with snapshots and encryption. Instance store volumes come with specific instance types as local NVMe disks — highest IOPS and lowest latency but ephemeral. Root volume is usually EBS; instance store appears as additional block devices mapped at launch.

entries.plainDefinition: Network block storage persisting independently of instance lifecycle.
Local NVMe/SSD tied to hardware — lost on stop or terminate.
entries.example: i3.large exposes 475 GB NVMe instance store.

entries.plainDefinition: Default EBS type — baseline IOPS and throughput configurable.
Incremental point-in-time backup stored in S3.
entries.example: Daily snapshot lifecycle to warm archive.

blocks.text: Choosing wrong storage causes data loss on stop/terminate or insufficient IOPS for databases. Snapshots enable backup and AMI creation for EBS only. Interview scenarios pit cost, durability, and performance tradeoffs.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: EBS = durable network disk with snapshots. Instance store = fast ephemeral — only with replication or cache workloads.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Durability requirement
items.body: Sole copy of data → EBS with snapshots. Cache/scratch → instance store OK.

items.title: Performance profile
items.body: Benchmark IOPS/latency — io2 for sustained DB, instance store for Kafka/Cassandra.

items.title: Lifecycle
items.body: Stop/start preserves EBS; instance store cleared on stop for most types.

items.title: Encrypt and attach
items.body: Enable encryption at rest with AWS KMS; attach data volumes at launch or runtime.

diagram.title: EBS vs instance store attachment
diagram.source:
flowchart LR
  EC2[EC2 instance]
  EC2 --> EBS[EBS gp3 root\npersists stop/start]
  EC2 --> IS[Instance store NVMe\nephemeral]
  EBS --> SNAP[EBS snapshot]
  IS --> X[Lost on stop/terminate]

snippet.label: Create encrypted gp3 volume and attach
snippet.code:
VOL=$(aws ec2 create-volume \
  --availability-zone ap-south-1a \
  --size 100 \
  --volume-type gp3 \
  --encrypted \
  --query VolumeId --output text)
aws ec2 attach-volume \
  --volume-id $VOL \
  --instance-id i-0app \
  --device /dev/sdf
snippet.explanation: Volume AZ must match instance AZ. Encrypt by default in production.

snippet.label: Snapshot EBS volume
snippet.code:
aws ec2 create-snapshot \
  --volume-id vol-0data \
  --description "nightly-db-backup"
aws ec2 describe-snapshots --owner-ids self --filters Name=volume-id,Values=vol-0data
snippet.explanation: Snapshots are incremental and stored durably — basis for DR and AMI.

snippet.label: Launch template block device mappings
snippet.code:
BlockDeviceMappings:
  - DeviceName: /dev/xvda
    Ebs:
      VolumeSize: 50
      VolumeType: gp3
      Encrypted: true
      DeleteOnTermination: true
  - DeviceName: /dev/xvdb
    Ebs:
      VolumeSize: 500
      VolumeType: io2
      Iops: 10000
snippet.explanation: Root gp3 plus io2 data volume. Instance store types use VirtualName not Ebs block.

snippet.label: List instance store devices
snippet.explanation: Confirm instance store presence before relying on local NVMe.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Storing sole database copy on instance store. Forgetting DeleteOnTermination=false loses data volumes on terminate. io1/io2 cost surprise without IOPS planning.

blocks.text: Multi-Attach io2 only for clustered filesystems (Oracle RAC patterns). How to prove it in production: CloudWatch VolumeQueueLength, VolumeReadOps/WriteOps, and fio benchmarks before production cutover.

blocks.title: Tradeoffs at senior level
rows: No durability — node loss = data loss

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Putting production database on instance store without replication gets rejected. Strong answer: EBS io2 + snapshots, or instance store only for replicated shards.

interviewTakeaways: EBS persists across stop/start; instance store is ephemeral on most instance types.
Snapshots and encryption apply to EBS — not instance store.
Match volume type to IOPS needs — gp3 default, io2 for databases.
60s: EBS durable + snapshots. Instance store fast ephemeral. DB on EBS or replicated on local NVMe.
Follow-up: what happens to instance store on reboot vs stop?
commonPitfalls: Database on instance store as sole copy — rejected.
Strong answer: EBS with snapshots or Cassandra/Kafka style replication on local disk.
Assuming all instance types have instance store.
Ignoring DeleteOnTermination on data EBS volumes.

jsTsCorrelations.note: os.tmpdir() on EC2 is local disk — like instance store scratch. EBS mounted /data is durable like a persistent volume in k8s.
Writing logs to instance store risks loss on replace — ship to CloudWatch Logs or S3 like centralized logging in Node apps.
